items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: when I was with the Basie band, and when I left the Basie band to join Duke

ctx.x: Yeah. I don’t know if everybody knows about this, but when I was with the Basie band, and when I left the Basie band to join Duke, you know I left, well we had kicked it around a little bit and he had sent his scouts around, John Sully, Al Sully and Evie, all the people would come around, and Joe, his little — Joe Morgan. He said “you want to join the band?” And I used to like his little hat that he used to wear. And he said “I’ll get you a hat like this if you’ll join.” So finally we talked about it long enough…
decided well I think I’d like to join Duke’s band. This is when, at this time, Basie was down to a quintet. So we were working in Chicago —

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I refer to my stint with the Basie band as the period during which I attended the prep school in preparation for enrollment at the University of Ellingtonia.

ctx.x: Okay. You characterized your time with Ellington as being like being in college, and you further said – just reading a quote – “I would say that probably the most outstanding thing was the period during which I worked with the Ellington band” in terms of maybe characterizing your career. Do you want to expand on those ideas?

I refer to my stint with the Ellington band as the period during which I attended the University of Ellingtonia, and that encompassed – every university has to have, what? Five schools. There were far more schools than that that you became well educated in at the University of Ellingtonia. I refer to my stint with the Basie band as the period during which I attended the prep school in preparation for enrollment at the University of Ellingtonia. So both those schools were – both bands were very, very important to…

What about the – what did – what was your – what is the – what was your learning that came from sitting in the trumpet section with Cat Anderson, Shorty Baker, Ray Nance, and others in the Ellington band?
